reasons: F01, F02, F04, F07: no material weakness, no going-concern doubt and no prior-period correction, so the card shows no direct sign of misstatement.
F05, F06, F14, F15: no auditor change, no disagreements with the accountants, and the CEO and CFO did not change, so governance looks stable.
F16, F17, F18, F19: no SEC inquiry, no class action, no other government investigation and no covenant problems.
F03: no auditor opinion on internal control was required, which is normal for a smaller bank filer. It means the controls get less outside checking, so I add a little risk.

F24: the critical audit matter is about reserves and estimates, most likely the allowance for credit losses. This is the main place a bank can use judgment to manage earnings, and it is usual for banks, so it adds only a little risk.
R08, R10, R19: accruals are near zero and operating cash flow is 1.19 times net income, so earnings are backed by cash.
R15, R05: ROA changed by only 0.01 and the depreciation index is 1.17. Neither is a strong warning sign.
R13: soft assets are 0.95 of total assets, which is expected for a bank because loans and securities make up most assets. It is not a red flag here.
R01-R04, R06, R07, R09, R17: most Beneish and Dechow ratios are n/a because they do not apply to a bank, so the ratio screen is weak evidence either way.

F21, R16, F20, F22, F23, F25, F26: a capital raise was planned (F21) but no securities were issued in the year (R16). There is no incentive pay tied to revenue or EPS, no major acquisition, no SPAC, no voluntary accounting change and no non-GAAP emphasis. The planned raise adds a little pressure, but very little.
guess: Skyline Bankshares, Inc. (formerly Parkway Acquisition Corp., parent of Skyline National Bank, Virginia)
